title: NeoWorld-Pro: Programming Interactive Scenes from Monocular Images for Embodied Simulation
claim: One generated simulation-ready scene supports many physical and interactive behaviors, with correct versus failed outcomes shown per component.
layout: Input and generated scene on top; arrows fan out to six panels (a-f)
description: The top left shows a rendered input image of a room with a door, bookshelf, clock, and desk. Next to it is the generated scene, with blue ellipses circling desk objects: a phone stand, a matchbox, a pen holder, and domino-like blocks. Blue gradient arrows run from these circles to six labeled panels. Panels (a) and (b) show drawer and matchbox opening with a hand icon and a motion arrow. Panels (c) and (d) are filmstrips of free fall and domino gravity, each with a 'Fail (Wrong Position)' column beside a 'Success' column. Panel (e) shows pen-insertion manipulation with 'Fail (Wrong Size)', 'Fail (Sub-optimal Policy)', and 'Success' columns. Panel (f) shows a four-frame sequence of a robot arm grasping a pen into a holder. The eye goes first to the large scene renders and then follows the arrows to the panels.
caption: Demonstration of NeoWorld-Pro. Our framework ensures simulation-readiness by optimizing: (a-b) physically plausible intra-object articulations under external forces, (c-d) stable inter-object spatial configurations, and (e-f) scene viability for assembly and manipulation tasks.
abstract: The advancement of Embodied AI necessitates high-quality simulation assets that faithfully mirror the real world. However, transforming raw visual observations into simulation-ready scenes remains challenging due to the lack of physical grounding and scene-level interactivity in current image-to-URDF methods. We propose NeoWorld-Pro, a framework that reformulates monocular scene reconstruction as procedural programming for interactive 3D environments. Leveraging the zero-shot reasoning and code synthesis capabilities of MLLMs, NeoWorld-Pro converts a single RGB image into executable programs specifying object geometry, articulation, and physical properties. A physics-in-the-loop mechanism then iteratively refines the generated programs by validating their execution in a physics engine, enforcing physically plausible articulations, valid object compositions and interactions, and accurate spatial relationships. Experiments show that NeoWorld-Pro outperforms open-loop and prior monocular reconstruction methods, while enabling complex downstream tasks such as stable stacking and fine-grained manipulation.
